conviction.label: Strong Bullish
conviction.thesis: RIL remains India's largest earnings compounder with optionality across telecom, retail and new energy.
reasons: Record Jio EBITDA with ARPU uptick signals pricing power and tariff-cycle gains flowing through.
Retail scaling digital commerce with 42% order growth and expanding store footprint.
New-energy vertical (solar, electrolysers, batteries) is a decade-long growth runway backed by $100B+ capex plan.
Zero promoter pledge and clean balance sheet allow debt-funded growth without shareholder dilution risk.
risks: O2C refining margins remain cyclical and weigh on consolidated margins.
FII stake trimming in recent quarters adds near-term supply pressure.
New-energy returns may take longer than market expects to become material.

conviction.label: Bullish
conviction.thesis: TCS offers best-in-class margin and cash-flow quality with a wide moat, though growth is cyclical.
reasons: Deal TCV remains strong ($10B+/quarter) with AI modernization contracts accelerating.
Attrition easing and utilization improving supports margin expansion runway.
48.6% RoE with ~100% dividend/buyback payout is shareholder-friendly.
Order pipeline from BFSI recovery and cloud migration is building.
risks: IT spending cycles could stay soft in discretionary segments.
28x P/E leaves little room for earnings disappointment.
Wage inflation and AI-driven pricing pressure in commoditised work.

conviction.label: Strong Bullish
conviction.thesis: Post-merger integration is nearly complete; the franchise is compounding deposits and loans with improving NIMs.
reasons: Deposit growth of 16% YoY and CASA normalizing post-merger.
NIM expected to stabilize as high-cost deposit repricing rolls off by Q3.
Asset quality remains among the best in Indian banking despite scale.
Institutional-heavy holding base and zero promoter risk add governance comfort.
risks: Unsecured retail watch-list rising needs monitoring.
Merger-related cost synergies may take longer to reflect in RoA.
Liquidity coverage ratio discipline can cap aggressive credit growth.

conviction.label: Bullish
conviction.thesis: Infosys pairs a fortress balance sheet with an improving AI-services pipeline and a fresh $2B buyback.
reasons: Large AI-focused deals signal willingness to pay for transformation.
Digital & cloud now over 60% of revenue with better margins.
$2B buyback plus 2.4% dividend yield supports the stock.
Cash conversion ~1.1x of profit with net cash of ~$2.5B.
risks: Legacy application maintenance revenue shrinking faster than new wins.
Visa policy tightening adds wage cost pressure in the US.
Euro/US demand softness in banking vertical.

conviction.label: Neutral
conviction.thesis: Blinkit is scaling impressively but valuation embeds years of perfection; quality of earnings needs watching.
reasons: Blinkit turned store-level profitable for the first time, validating the quick-commerce model.
GOV growth of 64% is real and backed by store expansion and order frequency.
Food delivery is consolidating with improved take rates.
Net cash balance sheet provides optionality for expansion.
risks: Competitive discount burn returning in quick commerce.
412x P/E prices in a decade of flawless execution.
Founder selling and senior exits create sentiment overhang.

conviction.label: Bullish
conviction.thesis: The largest PSU bank is delivering a clean asset-quality cycle with compelling value at 1.7x book.
reasons: GNPA at a 15-year low of 2.1% with strong provisioning buffer.
Profit growth of 24% on lower credit costs is sustainable for another year.
Deposit franchise and sovereign backing give structural stability.
10.2x P/E is inexpensive versus mid-teen RoE trajectory.
risks: Rates cycle and credit cost normalisation could slow profit growth.
CASA ratio pressure from competition for deposits.
Government ownership can invite capital-raise dilution risk.

conviction.label: Neutral
conviction.thesis: Steel cycle remains soft in Europe; the EU carbon-tax overhang caps re-rating despite India strength.
reasons: Indian operations are healthy with strong operating leverage at Kalinganagar.
Tata Steel UK faces structural cost issues and CBAM-related charges.
Balance sheet de-leveraging is on track with strong consolidated OCF.
Stock at 1.3x book reflects the cyclical pessimism already priced.
risks: EU carbon tax could structurally impair the Dutch/UK business.
Chinese export dumping pressure on steel prices.
2.4% promoter pledge is a small but real governance overhang.

conviction.label: Strong Bullish
conviction.thesis: Defence indigenisation is a multi-decade theme and HAL is the monopoly beneficiary with an all-time-high order book.
reasons: Order book of Rs 94,000 Cr (~4x revenue) provides decade-like revenue visibility.
97 Tejas Mk-1A order confirms the fighter-jet production ramp.
Strong RoE of 27.4% with near-zero leverage.
Government holding 71.5% makes it immune to promoter risk.
risks: Deliveries and revenue recognition can slip on certification delays.
38.6x P/E leaves little room for execution misses.
Capex and working-capital needs of scaling production.

conviction.label: Bearish
conviction.thesis: Recovery is real but slow, and regulatory risk keeps a lid on the re-rating until compliance stabilises.
reasons: UPI TPAP approval restores device onboarding and payments momentum.
Cost controls are narrowing losses faster than earlier guidance.
Buyback of Rs 1,600 Cr signals management confidence.
RBI compliance checks add an unpredictable regulatory variable.
risks: OCF remains negative; profit quality is not yet proven.
Fresh RBI compliance scrutiny could delay the payments recovery.
Competition from aggressive UPI aggregators caps monetisation.

conviction.label: Bearish
conviction.thesis: The portfolio grows, but cash-flow quality, pledge and governance scrutiny make it a high-risk speculative position.
reasons: New-energy and airports verticals are scaling with real traffic/order growth.
Group diversification lowers single-segment concentration risk.
OCF and FCF are negative while reported profits grow - a cash-quality red flag.
Ongoing SEBI investigation and related-party disclosures cap institutional appetite.
risks: Negative operating cash flow funds growth through debt.
SEBI investigation outcome is binary and unpredictable.
Promoter pledge of 7.4% increases leverage sensitivity.

conviction.label: Bullish
conviction.thesis: JLR's premium cycle plus India CV leadership create a strong earnings engine at an undemanding multiple.
reasons: JLR order book remains strong with healthy mix of Range Rover and Defender.
India CV market share gains and PV (Punch/Curvv) success broaden the base.
OCF of Rs 56,800 Cr funds deleveraging and EV capex.
8.6x P/E with 45% RoE is inexpensive for this growth.
risks: Global luxury demand and China weakness could hit JLR volumes.
EV transition in India is slower than company guidance.
Working-capital swings on dealer financing.

conviction.label: Bullish
conviction.thesis: ARPU-led growth, spectrum investment cycle payoff and deleveraging make Airtel a quality telecom compounder.
reasons: ARPU uptrend from tariff hikes flows almost entirely to EBITDA margin.
Mobile subscriber net adds positive after a long stagnation.
Africa operations turning profitable with data mix improving.
OCF of Rs 52,700 Cr comfortably covers capex and debt service.
risks: Regulatory uncertainty around floor tariffs and AGR.
87x P/E reflects elevated spectrum-capex cycle expectations.
Reliance Jio competitive intensity on pricing.

conviction.label: Bullish
conviction.thesis: The infra order super-cycle and working-capital discipline position L&T for margin-accretive growth.
reasons: Order inflow at record pace across infrastructure, energy and defence.
Working-capital days normalised, lifting OCF and FCF quality.
RoE improving toward mid-to-high teens on capital efficiency.
Diversified order book derisks single-segment cycles.
risks: Public capex slowdown if government spending tightens.
42.8x P/E is expensive; any order-book hiccup hurts.
Competitive pricing pressure in EPC tenders.

conviction.label: Bullish
conviction.thesis: Specialty ramp-up in the US plus India branded-generics leadership support durable mid-teens growth.
reasons: Specialty products growing at double digits with higher margins.
India formulations business leads the domestic market.
Healthy OCF and positive FCF fund R&D without leverage.
No governance overhangs; clean promoter record.
risks: US price erosion in legacy generics portfolio.
39x P/E prices in specialty success.
Regulatory plant inspections could disrupt supply.
